### Tested versions

Was able to reproduce on 4.6.1, 4.6, 4.5, and 4.5.beta1.
Not observed in 4.5.dev5 or lower (yet.)
Seems more prevalent on recent versions.

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 9 7950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 63.14 GiB memory

### Issue description

Godot produces:
ERROR: Another resource is loaded from path 'res://main.tscn::h2yge' (possible cyclic resource inclusion).
In a simple scene with one exported Curve resource.

I've tried a couple other resource types such as JSON and was able to replicate the error with little effort.
So it does not seem unique to only the Curve resource. I first observed the error with a custom resource type.

Was able to reproduce on 4.6.1, 4.6, 4.5, and 4.5.beta1.
Not observed in 4.5.dev5 or lower (yet.)
Seems more prevalent on recent versions.

Average save / load attempts required to observe error:
Godot 4.7.dev1 -- 7 save/load attempts
Godot 4.6.1.stable -- 7 save/load attempts
Godot 4.6.stable -- 7 save/load attempts
Godot 4.5.stable -- 14 save/load attempts
Godot 4.5.beta1 -- 14 save/load attempts; also sometimes get error:  ERROR: Task 'generate_thumbnails' already exists.

Godot 4.5.dev5 -- N/A (tried 20+ save/load attempts and did not see any errors.)
Godot 4.5.dev4 -- N/A (tried 20+ save/load attempts and did not see any errors.)
Godot 4.5.dev1 -- N/A (tried 20+ save/load attempts and did not see any errors.)
Godot 4.4.1stable -- N/A (tried 20+ save/load attempts and did not see any errors.)
Godot 4.4.stable -- N/A (tried 20+ save/load attempts and did not see any errors.)
Godot 4.3.stable -- N/A (tried 20+ save/load attempts and did not see any errors.)

### Steps to reproduce

Open the example project in engine of choice (4.6, 4.5, 4.4.)
Repeatedly create and remove the exported resource, saving the scene intermittently.
(I am not sure if the bug will occur without saving the scene.)
So far I've only seen this triggered by manually using the mouse to clear and add resource.
Using Undo/Redo commands has not triggered it for me.

Check console output logs -- sometimes the error is difficult to reproduce.
After anywhere from 5 to 20 tries you should see the error.

Once the error occurs once, it is more likely to repeat until the resource is cleared, the scene is saved, and the project/scene is reloaded.

items.title: Move method maps from `ClassDB` to `GDType`.

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
- Follow-up of #113586 
- Follow-up of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117474
- Works towards https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12323

Moves `MethodBind` maps from `ClassDB` to `GDType`, to make access more efficient and to consolidate typing.

This one is not as trivial as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117474 (some decisions which I'm commenting below), but also not nearly as complicated as #113586. Overall, it should be relatively painless with targeted reviews :)

### Notes

One thing of note is that a few classes currently accidentally bind the methods of supertypes (to the supertypes). For example:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/456bdea954ee24e48cb562bfbf531de1cd96e371/scene/resources/mesh.cpp#L2318

Can be seen in the docs under `Mesh` instead of `ArrayMesh`:

[docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_mesh.html#class-mesh-method-create-trimesh-shape](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_mesh.html#class-mesh-method-create-trimesh-shape)

This doesn't work anymore with the new approach, because `GDType` is finalized after `_bind_methods`.
To fix the specific issues, I decided to do the agnostic thing and move the bindings to where they're bound anyway (a practical no-op), with a comment for follow-ups to decide how to address it properly.

items.title: GLTF files can prevent PNG/SVG files from being imported on Arm systems
items.body:
### Godot version

Latest master 2a0aef5f0912b60f85c9e150cc0bfbeab7de6e40 but different behavior on master

### System information

macOS 13.3 arm64 (also happens on Ubuntu Linux arm64)

We have narrowed down the bug in the comments, it seems to only happen on ARM, not x86.

### Issue description

Some hard-to-isolate situations can cause other files like PNG files to be permanently unimported. In some cases this can be fixed by deleting the `.import` files, but in some cases Godot gets stuck and it refuses to even regenerate the `.import` files let alone perform the import.

One of these situations can be triggered by the GLTF files in the attached minimal reproduction project. Part of this issue is a regression since 4.0-stable, part of it also exists in 4.0-stable.

### Steps to reproduce

* Open the minimal reproduction project with the latest master.
* Double-clicking on any of the PNG files gives an error that the resource can't be opened.
<details>

```
  Failed loading resource: res://torch/text/baseColor_1.png. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  editor/editor_node.cpp:1263 - Condition "!res.is_valid()" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_OPEN
  Failed loading resource: res://torch/text/emissive_1.png. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  editor/editor_node.cpp:1263 - Condition "!res.is_valid()" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_OPEN
  Failed loading resource: res://torch/minecraft_torch_minecraft_torch.png. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  editor/editor_node.cpp:1263 - Condition "!res.is_valid()" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_OPEN
  Failed loading resource: res://torch/minecraft_torch_minecraft_torch_emissive.png. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  editor/editor_node.cpp:1263 - Condition "!res.is_valid()" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_OPEN
```

</details>

* Try deleting the `.glb` and `.gltf` files. Double-click on a PNG file. Same errors.
* Try restarting Godot after deleting the `.glb` and `.gltf` files. Double-click on a PNG file. Same errors.
* Try deleting the `.png.import` files. The PNG files will now import and load fine.
* Note: If the `.glb` and `.gltf` files are deleted before you start Godot for the first time, the PNG files load fine.
* It seems like a very serious bug in the import pipeline if something can cause a PNG file to never import.

---

Another problem that you can test in the same minimal reproduction project, this has regressions since 4.0-stable:

* Open the minimal reproduction project with the latest master.
* Double-click on the `.glb` file. The torch will be white. This is a regression, in Godot 4.0-stable the torch has the proper textures. In the console it prints these errors:
<details>

```
  Failed loading resource: res://torch/minecraft_torch_minecraft_torch_emissive.png. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp:3282 - glTF: Image index '0' couldn't be loaded with the name: minecraft_torch_emissive. Skipping it.
  Failed loading resource: res://torch/minecraft_torch_minecraft_torch.png. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp:3282 - glTF: Image index '1' couldn't be loaded with the name: minecraft_torch. Skipping it.
```

</details>

* Double-click on the `.gltf` file. Similarly, the torch will be white, a regression, and errors in the console. But also note how Godot creates 2 new PNG files when double-clicking on the `.gltf`.
    * First of all it's a bug that Godot tries to extract textures that are already separate files.
    * Second of all these are valid files, you can open them with GIMP, Firefox, etc, but Godot refuses to import them.
* Delete `icon.svg.import` in the root of the project. Now Godot will refuse to import `icon.svg`, and it does not generate the `icon.svg.import` file.
* Delete all `.png.import` files. Now Godot will import those, and it will also import `icon.svg`, and double-clicking on the `.glb` or `.gltf` files will result in the models having textures.
* Delete the `.glb.import` file. Try double-clicking it again and the texture will be white again.
* Delete `icon.svg.import` in the root of the project. Now Godot will refuse to import `icon.svg` (again), and it does not generate the `icon.svg.import` file (again).
* It seems like a very serious bug in the import pipeline if something can cause the `.import` files to not generate.

---

The first issue is also present in 4.0-stable, I have written some text about that collapsed:

<details>

* Open the minimal reproduction project with Godot 4.0-stable.
* Double-clicking on any of the PNG files gives an error that the resource can't be opened.
<details>

```
  Failed loading resource: res://torch/text/baseColor_1.png. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  editor/editor_node.cpp:1209 - Condition "!res.is_valid()" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_OPEN
  Failed loading resource: res://torch/text/emissive_1.png. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  editor/editor_node.cpp:1209 - Condition "!res.is_valid()" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_OPEN
  Failed loading resource: res://torch/minecraft_torch_minecraft_torch.png. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  editor/editor_node.cpp:1209 - Condition "!res.is_valid()" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_OPEN
  Failed loading resource: res://torch/minecraft_torch_minecraft_torch_emissive.png. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  editor/editor_node.cpp:1209 - Condition "!res.is_valid()" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_OPEN
```

</details>

* Try deleting the `.glb` and `.gltf` files. Double-click on a PNG file. Same errors.
* Try restarting Godot after deleting the `.glb` and `.gltf` files. Double-click on a PNG file. Same errors.
* Try deleting the `.png.import` files. The PNG files will now import and load fine.

</details>

### Minimal reproduction project

[wherearemyimports.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/11379941/wherearemyimports.zip)

items.title: Dynamic `GDScript` cannot resolve `class_name` in script
items.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot v4.3.stable

### System information

Windows 10.0.22631 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6109) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700KF CPU @ 3.80GHz (16 Threads)

### Issue description

When using the `GDScript` class to dynamically create a script, the `class_name` fails to resolve within the same script and results in the following error:

> Parser Error: Identifier not found: Foo

Attempting to save the script to a file and loading it using `load()` at run-time also doesn't work. Loading the same script statically when created in the editor works.

This is an issue when developing a code generator for Godot as testing it is impossible without dynamically creating classes. It is also a problem when creating GDScript-based mods.

### Steps to reproduce

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	var gdscript := GDScript.new()
	gdscript.source_code = "class_name Foo extends Resource

static func get_foo() -> Foo:
	return Foo.new()
"
	gdscript.reload()
	var foo : Variant = gdscript.new()
	print(foo)
```

[project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17686435/project.zip)

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
Fixes #76429
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12784

This PR adds a new property to MeshLibrary items: `use_custom_preview`. If disabled (default), the `preview` will not be saved with the resource. Instead the editor will auto-generate the previews every time the library is loaded and when it changes. This makes MeshLibrary resources much smaller, as the preview textures no longer get embedded 😬

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2223172/b2292fca-6f6b-4d4c-a7ae-b9712d47f664

It's not perfect, because when you change the mesh's material, not the mesh itself, the change will not be detected. You can however clear the preview manually and it will get auto-generated again.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2223172/a36f23ae-122e-450f-b64a-9a1dbcb5a2c6

Using `set_item_preview()` (bound) will automatically enable the `use_custom_preview`. Also I added an option that preserves the previous behavior of embedding previews:

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2223172/20e77606-943a-4a09-8362-70093b31b41a)

While this PR preserves API compatibility, if someone had custom previews in their MeshLibrary they need to enable `use_custom_preview` property for each item, otherwise the previews will be lost.

Also this PR needs testing with large MeshLibrary with complex meshes. I reworked preview generation to be much faster, but I don't know if it's sufficiently fast.

items.title: Animation Player FPS shows rounded integer but still internally stores float converted from Seconds
items.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]
- Not reproducible in: v4.2.1.stable.official [b09f793f5]

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable - Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS 22.04 - X11 - GLES3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 860M (nvidia; 535.183.01) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4710HQ CPU @ 2.50GHz (8 Threads)

### Issue description

**Context**

I am working with fractional FPS for animations, since I set frame time in ms (in Aseprite) then calculate the corresponding FPS for an Animated Sprite (1000/frame duration in ms), then use a converter ([Animated Sprite to Animation Player Convertor for Godot 4.0](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/1605)) from Animated Sprite to Animation Player animation. This leads to FPS such as 12.5 FPS for 80ms frames.

So far in Godot v4.2.1 I could enter either 12.5 FPS or 80ms at the bottom of the Animation Player to get the snapping I wanted:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1e4a464-a6c9-44e7-b960-ed587d2130bc)

**Issue**

Since Godot 4.3, the FPS field only allows entering an integer. Entering a float will round it and display the rounded integer. This leads to imperfect FPS such as 13 instead of 12.5, leading to snapping between frames (observe the vertical blue bar not being snapped to the start of a sprite square preview):

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8760cddd-8cca-450a-8966-6951215607f2)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fba2cfc-3335-431b-a9c4-733ebf7ed92d)

I need to switch back to Seconds, then enter 0.08 and then switch back to FPS to get 12.5 FPS internally:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0b76fa5-92ed-402a-ba22-03839b2797f1)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d57065e-c6f4-47d9-b677-1b4f8171df31)

However, note that the rounded value 13 FPS is still displayed:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/701d0aa8-2632-49ff-83c9-61a1910a2307)

although snapping shows we are really still at 12.5 FPS / 80ms:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64b833c1-8017-4cf6-a42a-55d737ac4fac)

This is confusing, and furthermore, trying to re-enter 13 FPS manually will not change the value to 13. However, entering a different value like 14, then the old value 13 again *will* force refresh to 13 instead of 12.5.

**Fix suggestion**

Revert to showing fractional FPS as before, since they are still stored internally as such as indirectly accessibly via setting Seconds, but this requires an extra step for the user.

Currently there is not even an up/down arrow widget to increase/decrease FPS by 1, so there is no big advantage in showing integers anyway (and we could still add an up/down arrow for people who really want to use integers if we want to).

### Steps to reproduce

- Create an Animation Player node with a dummy animation track (the easiest to test timeline snapping is to manually increase the animation duration near the clock icon at the top-right)
- In the Animation Player panel, try to change FPS to a fractional value like 12.5 => rounded to 13
- Move the timeline vertical bar around to test snapping. Add some keyframes there to remember the positions.
- Switch to Seconds, enter 0.08, switch back to FPS => see 13 but internally it's 12.5
- Move the timeline vertical bar around to test snapping. See how it ends at different positions that the previous keyframes.
- Enter 14 FPS, confirm, then 13 again, confirm (to force value refresh).
- Move the timeline vertical bar around to test snapping. See how it's now snapping to the previous keyframes.

N/A

items.title: Add the ability to expose nodes for direct access in instantiated scenes

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body: # (Updated 4/13/2026) Implements Exposed Nodes, a tool that allows scene authors to explicitly define which child nodes are visible and editable by default when a scene is instanced. - Closes [https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8266](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8266) Exposed nodes: - Appear at the instance root in the Scene Tree - Allow property modification - Propagate one instancing level - Can be re-exposed - Can be defined via Advanced Import Settings Related: - Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3248 - Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4265 - Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/9660 - Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5475 - Closes (?) https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7803 - Closes (?) https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/9536 # Examples Sample Project [mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17603057/mrp.zip) Example by @ptlthg https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/84018#issuecomment-3267406194 # Technical Overview ## Serialization Stored within the PackedScene: ``` [exposed path="VBoxContainer/PanelContainer/MarginContainer1/HBoxContainer/TitleLabel"] [exposed path="VBoxContainer/MarginContainer2/Content"] Similar to how Editable Children is saved: [editable path="..."] ``` ## Metadata (defined in Node.h) During `PackedScene::instantiate`: - The stored exposed NodePaths are resolved. - The corresponding nodes are marked with metadata. - `META_EXPOSED_IN_OWNER` - Marks that the node is declared exposed in the scene that owns it. - `META_MARKED_FOR_EXPOSURE` - Marked within the current scene that we want to expose or re-expose the node. - `META_EXPOSED_IN_INSTANCE` - Stores a reference to the highest-level instanced scene that re/exposes the node. - This encodes provenance and allows the editor to determine: 1. Whether the stored instance's owner matches the currently edited scene. 2. If not, the node is not surfaced. - `META_CONTAINS_EXPOSED_NODES` Stored on the owner as a fast-path optimization to avoid unnecessary subtree scans. The logic for each node marked for exposure in the packed scene during instatiation: - `GEN_EDIT_STATE_INSTANCE` - if the node is owned by this instance: - it’s marked with `META_EXPOSED_IN_OWNER`. - `META_EXPOSED_IN_INSTANCE` is set to the root node of this instance - if the node isnt owned by this instance, but is already an exposed node coming from a nested instance - Update `META_EXPOSED_IN_INSTANCE` to the root. - `GEN_EDIT_STATE_MAIN` - if the exposed node is owned by the currently edited scene - we marked it with `META_MARKED_FOR_EXPOSURE` ## Scene Tree Ordering Exposed nodes are always grouped before non-exposed local siblings. In order to achieve this `SceneTreeEditor::_move_node_children` has been modified to find and display the exposed nodes first. 1. Add all our exposed node tree items to a list. 2. Add all the normal nodes to the same list 3. Add them back to the tree in that order. To determine if a node is exposed and should be visible or not we use the following check: ```cpp bool is_exposed = child->has_meta(META_EXPOSED_IN_OWNER) && child->get_owner() == EditorNode::get_singleton()->get_edited_scene(); bool exposure_is_visible = false; if (child->has_meta(META_EXPOSED_IN_INSTANCE)) { Node *exposed_by = Object::cast_to(child->get_meta(META_EXPOSED_IN_INSTANCE)); exposure_is_visible = exposed_by != nullptr && exposed_by->get_owner() != nullptr && exposed_by->get_owner() == EditorNode::get_singleton()->get_edited_scene(); } is_exposed = is_exposed || exposure_is_visible; ``` Since Exposed nodes may originate from different internal subtrees if we were to allow users to place nodes between exposed nodes they could end up in an unexpected place visually. The rules from `SceneTreeDock::_normalize_drop_on_exposed_node` are defined below: | Requested Position | Final Position | | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | | (-1) above an exposed node | place after all exposed nodes within the nearest visible parent. | | (0) on an exposed node | place at end of that node's children | | (1) below an exposed node | place after all exposed nodes within the nearest visible parent. | | (2) as first child of exposed node | place after all exposed nodes. | ## Runtime Runtime scene structure is unchanged. Exposed nodes which contain child nodes or modified properties behave the same way Editable Children does. ## Performance Considerations & Improvements for the future - We have to do deep tree searches to find exposed nodes during `SceneTreeEditor::_update_node_subtree` and bubble them up. - `SceneTreeEditor::_move_node_children` is slower because it must find the exposed nodes first. ## What's left? - Fix bugs as they are found - Continue to test ## Key Discussion Comments These comments and notable replies from contributors/users provide an overview of the discussions around this PR. Since this PR is almost 3 years old and has close to 400+ entries I figured it would be helpful for any new reviewers to catch up. Please note that many of these links are just the start of a conversation and I encourage you to read the many replies stemming from them.
